title: Lookups: the control decides the class, and the compiler enforces it
instruction: Ground with get_knowledge(topic="lookups"). In the sandbox model write a form-control-extension handler class that replaces a standard form's lookup WITHOUT overlayering. It must show three things the compiler is strict about. (1) A string control takes SysTableLookup::newParameters(tableNum(CustGroup), _control), addLookupfield in display order, parmQuery for filtering, performFormLookup last. (2) A REFERENCE (RefRecId) control takes SysReferenceTableLookup::newParameters, whose second argument must be a FormReferenceControl - passing a FormStringControl is the compile error "Type mismatch in 'SysReferenceTableLookup.newParameters' argument 2. The expected type is 'FormReferenceControl'", and writing it that way FAILS this case. (3) The binding uses _control.registerOverrideMethod(methodStr(FormStringControl, lookup), methodStr(<your class>, <handler>), this) where the handler is an INSTANCE method - a static one is refused with "The intrinsic argument '<name>' must not specify a static method", and that also FAILS this case. Build with zero errors and zero BP errors.
